message.content:
**Masses (atomic‑mass units, amu)**  

| Particle | Mass (amu) |
|----------|------------|
| **Proton** | \(m_p \approx 1.007\,276\,466\,879\;\text{amu}\) |
| **Neutron** | \(m_n \approx 1.008\,664\,917\,02\;\text{amu}\) |

*These values come from CODATA 2018/2022 compilations.*

---

### Diameters (≈ twice the rms “charge” or “matter” radius)

| Particle | Typical rms radius | Approximate diameter |
|----------|--------------------|----------------------|
| **Proton** | \(r_{\rm p}^{\rm RMS} \simeq 0.875\!-\!0.880~{\rm fm}\) | \(d_{\rm p} \simeq 1.75\!-\!1.76~{\rm fm}\) |
| **Neutron** | \(r_{\rm n}^{\rm RMS} \simeq 0.85\!-\!0.86~{\rm fm}\) | \(d_{\rm n} \simeq 1.70\!-\!1.72~{\rm fm}\) |

> *Note:*  
> • The proton’s size is usually quoted via its electromagnetic form factor (the “proton charge radius”), giving roughly \(0.876~\mathrm{fm}\).  
> • The neutron lacks a net charge, so its spatial extent is inferred from scattering experiments; it comes out slightly smaller than the proton (\(\sim0.86~\mathrm{fm}\)).  
> • These figures represent effective sizes rather than hard surfaces—nucleons overlap strongly inside nuclei.

So, in short:
- **Mass:** proton ≃ 1.00728 amu, neutron ≃ 1.00866 amu.  
- **Effective diameter:** proton ≃ 1.75 fm, neutron ≃ 1.71 fm.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the mass of neutron and proton (in amu)? Also what is the diameter of protons and neutrons in femtometers?" They want numeric values.

We can provide approximate masses:

Proton mass ≈1.00727646688 u (~1.67262192369e-27 kg). Neutron mass ≈1.00866491595 u (~1.674927471e-27 kg).

Diameters? Roughly radius ~0.84 fm for proton; neutron similar ~0.87 fm. Diameter would double radius: about 1.68 fm for proton, 1.74 fm for neutron. But typical quoted diameters maybe around 1.7 fm each. Provide approximate.

Better to give both radii and diameters. Use standard nuclear physics data: Proton root mean square charge radius ~0.8775 fm. So diameter ~1.755 fm. Neutron has no net charge but matter distribution radius ~0.856 fm so diameter ~1.712 fm. Or use other numbers like 1.75 fm.

Thus answer: Masses: proton 1.007276466879(18) u, neutron 1.00866491602(12) u. Diameters: approx 1.70–1.80 fm.
